problem: The step says compaction 'drops overwritten versions' unconditionally. BigTable keeps multiple versions per cell, and old versions are removed only by per-family garbage-collection rules. As written it contradicts Section 1 and teaches that a newer write makes older versions unreadable.
fix: Compaction merges SSTables and removes versions only when the family's garbage-collection rules allow, for example beyond the version count or age limit.

problem: It says that with key www.cnn.com 'pages of one site would scatter'. Pages on the same host www.cnn.com all share the prefix www.cnn.com, so they stay together. Reversing the host groups different cnn.com subdomains under com.cnn.
fix: If keys kept hostnames unreversed, pages from different cnn.com subdomains such as www, sports and money would sort apart; reversing puts all cnn.com hosts under com.cnn.

where: Section 4, crawler paragraph and worked example
problem: 'One tablet scan reads the whole site' is imprecise. A large site can span multiple tablets; a range scan may read several adjacent tablets, not a single tablet.
fix: A range scan reads the rows contiguously; a large site spans several adjacent tablets.

problem: The row org.wiki has cell 'b1' even though the spec says cells hold a version timestamp; b1 is not a timestamp label. This looks like a typo and confuses the figure.
fix: Use a timestamp label such as t1, or relabel the cell as a value if that is intended.

problem: Saying 'Cloud databases generalise the trade: drop joins and fixed schemas' overgeneralises. Cloud relational databases keep joins and schemas; the statement is true only for the NoSQL cloud databases discussed here.
fix: The NoSQL cloud databases in this unit generalise the trade: they drop joins and fixed schemas to scale out.
